> **Alpha release.** An early alpha for testing: expect rough edges and changes between versions, and try it on lab or non-critical routers first.

Second alpha of **Wingox**, the MikroTik RouterOS 7 manager that reaches routers through a proxy. This one adds settings, saved workspaces and links to the official documentation.

## New

- **Settings** (gear icon in the header), saved automatically on this computer:
  - **Appearance:** theme (dark, light, or follow Windows), accent color, interface and data fonts (JetBrains Mono, Cascadia Code, Consolas…), interface size 80–150 %, table density.
  - **Terminal:** font size, cursor style and blinking, scrollback.
  - **Behaviour:** the section a device opens on, the monitor interval, confirm "Close all", reset column widths.
  - **Notifications:** Windows notifications, also when a device comes back, alert sound.
- **Workspaces** (in the tab bar):
  - Save the open sessions under a name: every tab with its panes and sections, the active tab, and detached windows with their position and size.
  - Reopen them later as they were. Passwords are never stored in a workspace; tabs refer to your saved devices.
  - On reopening, terminals connect again and tables reload.
- **Official documentation per section.** A book icon on every pane opens that section's page in MikroTik's official RouterOS documentation (help.mikrotik.com), at the exact heading: for example DHCP → "DHCP Server", or Bridging → "Port Settings".

## Changed

- Themes: only **dark** and **light** remain. Accent colors in Settings replace the old terminal and amber themes; if you used one of those, Wingox starts in dark.

## Download (Windows 10/11, x64)

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Wingox_…_x64-setup.exe` | installer (recommended) |
| `Wingox_…_x64_en-US.msi` | MSI installer, for managed deployments |
| `wingox-0.1.0-alpha.2-windows-x64-portable.exe` | portable, no install (needs WebView2, already on Windows 10/11) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | checksums |

The binaries are **not code-signed**: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run ("More info" → "Run anyway"). Your saved devices, settings and workspaces are kept when you update.

## Known limitations

- RouterOS 7 only (REST API); the binary API and RouterOS 6 come later.
- Device passwords are stored in a JSON file in the app's config folder (`%APPDATA%\com.eirikrrrr.wingox`), not yet in the Windows credential store.
